title: Real-time projection layer to smooth console usage charts during backfill jitter
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Console usage charts (per-tenant and per-model sparklines) show visible, confusing jumps when late/batched backfill events arrive. This ticket adds a transient projection layer and visual hints that preserve short-term chart stability while still surfacing accurate backfilled totals once reconciliations complete.
goal: Reduce user-facing chart jitter for short windows (1min–6hr) by presenting an explainable projection until authoritative backfill reconciles; keep final accounting unchanged and auditable.
observations: Late ingest/backfills commonly arrive in bursts after shard replays or ledger reprocessing, producing stepwise spikes in 1m and 5m console charts.
Customers interpret spikes as production traffic changes; SREs and billing teams get support noise.
Current work to reconcile ledgers is correct but asynchronous — UI needs a UX-safe interim representation.
Existing smoothing logic is naive (fixed moving average) and can obscure real regressions or rollbacks.
approach_summary: Implement an ephemeral projection service that emits provisional usage deltas for UI clients for short horizons (up to 6 hours).
Projection algorithm: weighted exponential smoothing + monotonic prefix enforcement + uncertainty bands; tuned to avoid masking >10% real delta in the last 10 minutes.
Show visual indicators on charts: 'Projected' shading and a small badge when data is provisional; animate transitions when backfill arrives to avoid abrupt jumps.
Record both provisional and authoritative values in the console telemetry so account reconciliation is auditable.
Keep projections off for tenants with legal/compliance hooks that require raw ingest visibility (configurable per-tenant flag).
Expose a debug toggle for internal support to see raw event streams vs projected series.
Do not alter billing ledgers or quota calculations; this is purely a UI/observability layer.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Dashboard 1m/5m per-model and per-tenant sparklines show reduced jump amplitude for at least 80% of simulated late-backfill scenarios in our synthetic testbed.
2) Provisional vs authoritative series are stored as separate metrics and visible in the console timeline explorer.

3) When a backfill arrives, the UI transitions smoothly (animated interpolation) from projected to authoritative value; no >30% instantaneous visual delta for top-tier customers during rollout in canary.
4) No changes to billing/ledger pipelines; all accounting systems unchanged and audits still reconcile to authoritative totals.
5) Feature flag to disable projections per-tenant is implemented; enabled by default for self-serve tenants.
6) Observability: sentinel alerts for projection model drift (if projection error > threshold for 3 hours) are wired into PagerDuty.
7) Unit/integration tests for projection algorithm and a synthetic backfill harness are included in the PR.
8) UX copy and 'provisional' indicator approved by Design and PM.
9) Documentation page in Console docs describing projection behavior and the indicator is published and linked from the UI.
10) Performance: projection layer adds <5ms median latency to chart API responses and scales horizontally with existing console stateless pool.
work_items: WIP: design API surface for chart projection (console API v2 query param & response flags)
Implement projection microservice (stateless, in Go) that subscribes to reconstructed short-window aggregates
Add provisional flag and shading metadata to chart API payloads
Design: create visual 'Projected' treatment and animation spec
Integration tests: synthetic late-backfill generator and end-to-end UI snapshot tests
Feature flag gating and per-tenant opt-out control in admin console
Docs + support playbook + internal debug toggle
Canary rollout to 5% accounts then 25% then global; monitor error & support signals
risks: Projection could mask an actual rapid production regression if tuned too aggressively — mitigated via conservative thresholds and uncertainty bands.
Added UI complexity could confuse users if indicator isn't prominent or copy is unclear.
Extra service adds operational cost and another failure mode for console; ensure fallback to raw series on service error.
Edge case: tenants with very spiky traffic patterns may see projection error > threshold; will be tracked by drift alerts and opt-out.
Need coordination with billing/ledger owners to ensure we never accidentally write provisional numbers to accounting systems.
SLA: projection service must not increase console API latency beyond budget.
Security: projected data must obey tenant-scoping and RBAC; ensure per-tenant opt-out honors compliance cases.
implementation_notes: Projection algorithm prototype implemented in python prototype/console_proj.ipynb — port to Go for production.
Leverage existing short-window aggregations (1m/5m) from metrics pipeline; avoid re-ingesting raw token events for cost reasons.
Store provisional series in time-series DB as a separate metric name with a _provisional suffix for auditability.
When authoritative delta arrives, emit a reconciliation event that the UI consumes to trigger animated interpolation.
Provide an opt-out header X-Console-Projections: disable for debug or compliance requests.
PR must include load test showing <5ms added latency at 95th percentile for current traffic volume.
Coordinate with Design (Lina Gomez) for visuals and with PM (Jonas Richter) for messaging.
Prepare runbook for support to explain projection behavior to customers (include step-by-step to disable per-tenant).
Data retention: keep provisional metrics for 30 days to support investigations then a TTL purge.
Follow-up: evaluate if projection can be applied to other console charts (cost heatmaps) after rollout.
